messages:
alex: Noticing elevated 5xxs for hosted text-generation in us-west-2 beginning ~05:05 UTC. Error spike concentrated on cache-read path. Opening an incident thread. https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/1864701123
claire: oncall. I've put a soft throttle on non-critical streaming routes and enabled fallback to the nearest dedicated pool for high-priority customers. Error rate down from ~6.2% to ~2.1% after throttle.
ops-bot: monitor: detected increased kv-cache miss ratio and p99 read latency on cache-cluster-west. Alert id=kv-read-8921.
oncall: gathering logs now. early sign is a gradual increase in small-read latency tied to a background compaction job on the cache nodes.
claire: coordinated with infra to pause compaction on the affected shard and started a targeted restart for cache node i-0a7b3. Paused compaction should reduce IO pressure.
support: sent an interim update to impacted hosted customers: "We're aware of degraded generation performance in us-west-2 and have applied temporary mitigations. We'll provide updates as we make progress."
alex: mitigation checklist: 1) throttle non-critical streams (done), 2) enable dedicated fallback for select routes (done), 3) pause compaction (in progress), 4) targeted cache node restart (in progress), 5) customer outreach (done).
ops-bot: deploy-bot: cache-control: compaction pause applied to shard-7, restart scheduled for i-0a7b3, job=restart-452.
oncall: after the restart p95 latency improved and 5xxs dropped to ~0.6%. We'll keep monitoring for 60 minutes before restoring normal compaction schedule.
claire: marking incident severity=SEV3. We'll produce a short postmortem covering compaction timing and safeguards to prevent cascading queue pressure. Final incident doc link: https://go.redwood/incident/1864701123/summary
